name: Materials Science & Engineering
description: How the structure of materials, from atoms to microstructure, controls their properties, and how processing and selection turn metals, ceramics, polymers, composites and functional materials into reliable, high-performance products.

chapters.name: Introduction to Materials
chapters.summary: A first tour of what materials are, the main material classes, and how structure, properties, processing and performance are linked, using everyday objects.

topics.name: What materials science and engineering is (and how it differs from chemistry and physics)
The materials tetrahedron: structure, properties, processing and performance
The material classes: metals, ceramics, polymers, composites, semiconductors and biomaterials
Length scales of structure: atoms, crystals, grains, microstructure and components
Families of properties
Why a paperclip bends, a mug shatters and a bottle stretches: property differences explained by bonding
Everyday case studies: drink cans, smartphone glass, bicycle frames, tyres and non-stick pans
How materials are made: an overview of casting, shaping, joining and finishing
Units, orders of magnitude and reading a simple property chart (strength vs density)
Materials failures in the news: why bridges, pipes and aircraft parts fail
Materials and the environment: resources, energy and recycling at a glance
Careers and sub-fields in materials science and engineering

chapters.name: Materials in Human History & Society
chapters.summary: How the discovery and mastery of materials, from flint to silicon, shaped civilisations, economies and warfare.

topics.name: Stone, bone and fibre: the earliest engineered materials
Ceramics and pottery: firing clay and the first kilns
The Bronze Age: smelting copper and tin alloying
The Iron Age: bloomeries, wrought iron and early steel (wootz, Damascus, tatara)
Glass from antiquity to the float process
Concrete from Rome to Portland cement
The Industrial Revolution: Bessemer and open-hearth steel, aluminium by electrolysis
The polymer age: Bakelite, nylon and the plastics boom
The silicon age: transistors, integrated circuits and optical fibre
Materials in war and flight: armour, jet engines and the space race
Critical materials, geopolitics and supply chains today

chapters.name: Atomic Structure, Bonding & Solid-State Chemistry
chapters.summary: Explains how electrons bind atoms into solids and how bond type controls melting point, stiffness, expansion and conductivity.

topics.name: Atomic structure: electrons, orbitals, quantum numbers and electron configurations
The periodic table and periodic trends (radius, ionisation energy, electronegativity)
Ionic bonding, lattice energy and the Born-Haber cycle
Covalent bonding: Lewis structures, VSEPR, hybridisation and molecular orbitals
Metallic bonding and the free-electron picture
Secondary bonding: van der Waals, dipole interactions and hydrogen bonds
Interatomic force and potential-energy curves (Lennard-Jones, Morse)
Linking bond energy to melting point, elastic modulus and thermal expansion
From molecular orbitals to energy bands: metals, semiconductors and insulators
Mixed bonding and the bonding triangle (van Arkel-Ketelaar)
Introduction to solid-state reactions, stoichiometry and chemical kinetics
Acids, bases, oxidation-reduction and solutions for materials engineers

chapters.name: Crystal Structures
chapters.summary: Describes how atoms pack into the crystal structures of metals, ceramics and polymers, and how to index directions and planes.

topics.name: Crystalline versus amorphous solids
Lattices, bases and unit cells; the seven crystal systems and 14 Bravais lattices
Metallic crystal structures: FCC, BCC and HCP; coordination number and packing factor
Close-packed planes and stacking sequences (ABAB, ABCABC)
Density calculations from crystal structure
Miller indices for directions and planes; Miller-Bravais indices for hexagonal crystals
Linear and planar densities; slip-relevant planes
Interstitial sites (tetrahedral and octahedral) and radius-ratio rules
Ceramic crystal structures: rock salt, CsCl, zinc blende, fluorite, perovskite, spinel, corundum
Silicate structures and carbon allotropes (diamond, graphite, fullerenes)
Polymorphism and allotropy (iron, carbon, SiO2, ZrO2)
Polycrystals, grains, texture and anisotropy
Polymer crystallinity: chain folding and spherulites

chapters.name: Crystallography & Diffraction
chapters.summary: Covers the symmetry language of crystals and the diffraction theory used to determine structure from X-ray, electron and neutron scattering.

topics.name: Symmetry operations: rotation, reflection, inversion, screw axes and glide planes
Point groups and crystal classes; Hermann-Mauguin notation
Space groups and reading the International Tables for Crystallography
Stereographic projection and Wulff nets
Vector and matrix treatment of lattices; metric tensor; zone axes and the Weiss zone law
The reciprocal lattice and its relation to lattice planes
Bragg's law, the Laue equations and the Ewald sphere
Atomic scattering factors and the structure factor; systematic absences
Diffraction intensities: multiplicity, Lorentz-polarisation, temperature (Debye-Waller) factors
Powder diffraction patterns and indexing cubic and non-cubic crystals
Comparison of X-ray, electron and neutron diffraction
Quasicrystals and incommensurate structures
Tensor properties of crystals and Neumann's principle (anisotropy of conductivity, elasticity, piezoelectricity)

chapters.name: Defects in Crystals & Dislocations
chapters.summary: Introduces point, line, planar and volume defects, which control diffusion, strength, conductivity and almost every useful property.

topics.name: Why real crystals are imperfect: the thermodynamic necessity of vacancies
Point defects in metals: vacancies, self-interstitials and equilibrium concentration
Impurities and solid solutions: substitutional, interstitial and the Hume-Rothery rules
Point defects in ionic crystals: Schottky and Frenkel defects, charge neutrality, Kröger-Vink notation
Composition specification: weight and atom percent conversions

topics.name: Slip systems in FCC, BCC and HCP metals
Interfacial defects: grain boundaries (low and high angle), twin boundaries, phase boundaries and surfaces
Bulk defects: pores, cracks, inclusions and precipitates
Observing defects: etch pits, TEM contrast and grain-size measurement (ASTM grain size)
Defect-property relationships: how defects govern strength, diffusion and conductivity

chapters.name: Thermodynamics of Materials

Entropy and the second law; statistical interpretation of entropy
Gibbs and Helmholtz free energies; conditions for equilibrium

Maxwell relations and thermodynamic identities
Unary phase equilibria: Clausius-Clapeyron equation and one-component phase diagrams

Ideal, regular and non-ideal solutions; activity and activity coefficients

Gibbs phase rule
Reaction equilibria, equilibrium constants and Ellingham diagrams
Thermodynamics of point defects
Surfaces and interfaces: surface energy and capillarity (Gibbs-Thomson effect)
Introduction to statistical thermodynamics: partition functions and Einstein/Debye solids
